title: Power loss while the epoch-close record is written: the torn tail is truncated, every acked record stays

preconditions.notes: Four writes are level-1 acked and the epoch close has started: a 24-byte length prefix is on disk followed by only six body bytes, so the newest record has no complete len/crc32c (wal.md section 10 step 2).

timeline.event: four writes acked; one step open
power loss during the epoch-close record write
timeline.detail: a complete length prefix and a short body: the record cannot be parsed and nothing follows it
every process start is a cold recovery (wal.md section 10 step 4)
truncation stops at the last complete record and is logged with boot id, segment, byte offset and dropped bytes; it is not an error
every acked mseq is still present with the identical mutation and the materialized copy equals the replay
reconcile lists exactly the interrupted step of the pre-kill snapshot

notes: The distinction the runner must implement: a torn record at the TAIL is truncated and logged; a CRC failure that is not at the tail, or an invalid record followed by a valid one, is WAL_CORRUPT and the host enters Failed. The fixture asserts the first case only; the second has no fixture in the Swift suite and is therefore not lifted here.
